# Domain reference: Operations / Supply Chain

Job family covered: Operations Manager, Supply Chain Manager, Logistics Manager, Production Manager, Operations Director, COO, Buyer, Quality Manager.

---

## Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior / Coordinator | Experienced / Operations Manager | Senior / Operations Director | Leadership / COO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operational management | Executes processes, tracks indicators, reports anomalies. | Optimizes flows, handles contingencies, manages operational KPIs. | Restructures operations, industrializes processes, manages overall performance. | Defines the operational strategy, aligns operations with the business strategy. |
| Flow & supply chain management | Understands the logistics chain, places orders, tracks inventory. | Optimizes procurement, negotiates with suppliers, manages forecasts. | Designs the supply chain strategy, leads transformations (S&OP, lean, automation). | Manages the supply chain at group level, handles geopolitical and supplier risks. |
| Continuous improvement | Identifies dysfunctions, proposes one-off improvements. | Sets up structured approaches (lean, 5S, kaizen). Measures results. | Deploys a continuous improvement culture, trains teams, leads transformation projects. | Establishes operational excellence as a strategic discipline. |

## Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Description by level |
|---|---|
| Supplier & purchasing management | Junior: tracks orders. Experienced: negotiates, evaluates, diversifies the supplier panel. Senior: defines the purchasing strategy, leads strategic partnerships. |
| Quality management | Junior: applies procedures. Experienced: handles non-conformities, leads audits. Senior: defines the quality policy, certifications. |

## Complementary competencies (x1)

| Competency | Description |
|---|---|
| ERP & tools | Mastery of management tools (SAP, Oracle, WMS, TMS). Ability to lead implementation projects. |
| Health, safety & environment | HSE, regulatory compliance, CSR (RSE, corporate social responsibility) applied to operations. |
| Project management | Leading cross-functional projects (relocation, setting up a new site, IT migration). |

---

## Recommended role-play scenarios

- **Supplier crisis management**: a critical supplier announces a 3-week delay on an essential order. Ask the candidate to structure their response: immediate actions, plan B, internal communication, supplier negotiation. Observe: composure, methodology, ability to prioritize.
- **Process optimization**: present a logistics process with data (lead times, costs, error rates) and ask the candidate to identify bottlenecks and propose quantified improvements. Observe: analytical mind, pragmatism, knowledge of methodologies.

## Red flags

### Red
- No reference to measurement or KPIs in their practice
- Unable to describe a process end to end
- Systematically blames suppliers or teams without stepping back

### Orange
- Focus on execution with no improvement vision
- Difficulty quantifying the impact of their actions
- No curiosity about continuous improvement methodologies
